A measurable repeat sign-in requires Firebase Auth’s last-sign-in timestamp to be more than five minutes after the account-creation timestamp. Zero does not mean nobody returned: users may stay signed in, return through an existing session, use tools or games without a fresh authentication event, or use shared student links. Firebase Auth cannot reliably measure all repeat visits. Verified engagement means a measurable save, collection, or qualifying sign-in and is not total engagement.

Traffic quality / cluster context

Traffic quality matters more than raw volume alone. Market signals should be interpreted using volume + concentration + return behavior + signal type: how much traffic occurred, whether it clustered around one event, whether the same users/devices returned later, and whether activity represents student reach, mixed instructional use, or teacher/commercial intent.
Observed clusterConcentration and returnDecision-useful interpretation
Theresa, NYSept. 15 spike; 13 of 16 IDs returned later (81%)Strong sustained classroom adoption. Activity is overwhelmingly free, student-facing Word Wizard, Word Forge, and Spellbound use, with some Google Classroom referrals. This is student reach, not direct buyer intent; no teacher account is confirmed yet.
WisconsinSept. 15 cluster; 4 of 20 IDs returned (20%)Probable literacy-specialist, PD, or professional-network exposure. Multiple literacy educators from six school systems created accounts within roughly one hour. Low save counts are not failure; monitor downstream district signups and student traffic.
Illinois40 of 78 sessions on Sept. 30; 31 IDs; no observed returns through Oct. 2Too recent to judge retention. Could be classroom use, PD, or another shared-resource event.
Leinster, Ireland46 of 76 sessions on Sept. 23; 46 IDs; no later same-ID returnsLikely coordinated one-time event such as a class, training, presentation, or shared resource; not sustained adoption yet.
Virginia38 of 68 sessions on Sept. 18; 38 IDs; no later same-ID returnsLikely one-off campaign/shared-link event. Existing behavior was shallow and does not establish sustained school demand.

Student reach / adoption

Word Wizard, Word Forge, and Spellbound are free, student-facing homepage games. High use is valuable for classroom adoption and school-cluster detection, but is not a direct purchase signal.

Mixed instructional use

Robot Word Builder, Reading Word Spinner, Digital Reading Flashcards, and Comprehension Spinner may be student-facing but are often teacher-directed. Use depth, repeat behavior, and context before inferring commercial intent.

Teacher / commercial and need signals

Teacher Tools, Teacher Dashboard, Phoneme Counter, Letterbox Lesson, Plus Subscriptions, and state pages are stronger commercial-intent signals. Assessments and fluency indicate high need or potential intent, not automatic purchase intent; some visitors may expect a free tool before encountering the Plus gate.
